flashcard_questions.q: What does the atomic number of an element tell you?
flashcard_questions.a: The number of protons in the nucleus.

flashcard_questions.q: What makes two atoms isotopes of the same element?
flashcard_questions.a: The same number of protons but a different number of neutrons.

flashcard_questions.q: What is an alpha particle made of?
flashcard_questions.a: Two protons and two neutrons — a helium nucleus.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is the most ionising but least penetrating?
Which type of nuclear radiation is stopped by a thin sheet of aluminium?
Which type of nuclear radiation is the most penetrating but least ionising?
How does a beta particle form inside the nucleus?
flashcard_questions.a: A neutron splits into a proton and a high-speed electron.

flashcard_questions.q: In alpha decay the mass number falls by ____ and the atomic number falls by ____.
In beta decay, what happens to the atomic number?
Which isotope is produced when uranium-238 undergoes alpha decay?
What is the half-life of a radioactive isotope?
flashcard_questions.a: The time for the number of unstable nuclei in a sample to halve.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the unit of activity of a radioactive source?
A sample falls from 8000 Bq to 1000 Bq in 30 days. What is its half-life?
Does a person who has been irradiated become radioactive themselves?
flashcard_questions.a: No — irradiation exposes them to radiation but leaves no radioactive material behind.

notes: 15 cards: 4 term→definition (atomic number, isotopes, half-life, becquerel), 2 cloze on nuclear rules (neutron count, alpha decay 4/2), 3 property-to-radiation-type cards with uniquely identifying fronts to avoid alpha/beta/gamma interference, 2 process cards (beta formation, beta atomic number), 1 decay product, 1 half-life calculation using the lesson's worked values, 1 contamination/irradiation distinction. Dropped the atom and nucleus radius values and the carbon-14 decay example to stay inside 15.
